**Quiz 0001, attempt s1: 2 correct, 2 partial, 2 wrong.** Full feedback for each answer is in `grades/0001-s1.json`.

| Item | Verdict | Why | Misconception |
|---|---|---|---|
| q1 | Correct | The loop is what makes it an agent. | |
| q2 | Wrong | The model requests a tool call; your program opens the booking system. | M4 |
| q3 | Correct | A step limit stops a stuck loop. | |
| q4 | Wrong | There are 4 model calls: one for each of the 3 tool requests, plus one for the final answer. | M4 |
| q5 | Partial | You said the result goes back to the model, but not why: so it can choose the next step or write the answer. | |
| q6 | Partial | Tool descriptions are right; automatic memory of earlier sessions is wrong. | M3 |

**The main flaw:** you're treating the model as the thing that does the work. It only produces a request. Your program runs the tool, puts the result into the model's input and calls the model again. This affects your design and your budget, because every one of those calls costs money.

I also added learning records 0003 (M4) and 0004 (M3) and updated `NOTES.md`. These reflect s1 only; your later attempt, `s2`, is still ungraded, so they may not describe where you are now. I couldn't run a parse check on the grades file because the command was blocked.

**Your one next step:** trace the request "Book the laser cutter for me tomorrow at 3 pm" on paper. Assume the assistant checks the calendar and then makes the booking, one tool per model call. Label every step **MODEL** or **PROGRAM**, then count the model calls. Send me your trace and I'll check it.
